issues.description: The Stock.getStockIngredients() method has different return types between the template and the solution. In the template repository Stock.getStockIngredients() returns List<StockIngredient> (template expects a List), while in the solution repository it returns StockIngredient[] (an array). The problem statement's UML does not specify this getter, so students may be confused which form to use and this mismatch could cause compilation/test failures depending on which signature the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of getStockIngredients() consistent across template and solution. Prefer exposing the underlying array (StockIngredient[]) or the List<StockIngredient> in all artifacts. Update the template Stock.java to return StockIngredient[] (or update the solution to return List<StockIngredient>) and adjust any usages accordingly so students have a single, consistent API to implement against.
